title: Statistics and regression
summary: Sampling, measures of centre and spread, outliers and box plots, Pearson’s correlation coefficient and least-squares regression lines.

keyterms.definition: The whole group of interest from which a sample is taken.
A sample in which every member of the population has an equal chance of selection.
Discrete data take separate countable values; continuous data can take any value in a range.
The sum of the values divided by the number of values, x̄ = ∑x / n.
The middle value of ordered data (the mean of the two middle values when n is even).
IQR = Q₃ − Q₁, the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
A value more than 1.5 × IQR below Q₁ or above Q₃.
A measure of spread around the mean; the square root of the variance.
Correlation coefficient measuring the strength and direction of linear correlation, −1 ≤ r ≤ 1.
The least-squares line of y on x, used to predict y from x; it passes through (x̄, ȳ).
Predicting outside the range of the data; unreliable compared with interpolation.

questions.explanation: Six values: the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th, (9 + 11)/2.

questions.text: An outlier is a value more than 1.5 × IQR above Q₃ or below ___.
questions.explanation: The fences are Q₁ − 1.5 × IQR and Q₃ + 1.5 × IQR.

questions.statement: Adding 5 to every data value increases the standard deviation by 5.
questions.explanation: Adding a constant shifts every value equally, so the spread is unchanged; only the mean increases by 5.

questions.prompt: A data set has Q₁ = 12 and Q₃ = 20. Which value would be an outlier?
questions.explanation: IQR = 8, so the fences are 0 and 32. Only 35 lies outside.

questions.prompt: Every value in a data set is multiplied by 3. What happens?
options: The mean is multiplied by 3; the SD by 9
The mean is multiplied by 3; the SD is unchanged
The mean and the standard deviation are both multiplied by 3
questions.explanation: Scaling stretches the spread too. The variance is multiplied by 9.

questions.text: A sample in which every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen is a simple ___ sample.

questions.statement: The number of siblings a student has is discrete data.
questions.explanation: It can only take whole-number values.

questions.prompt: Match each sampling method to its description.

pairs.right: Every member equally likely to be chosen
Every kth member from an ordered list
Subgroups sampled in proportion to their size

questions.explanation: Convenience sampling is quick but likely to be biased.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to draw a box plot.
items: Find the minimum, Q₁, median, Q₃ and maximum
Draw the box from Q₁ to Q₃ and add whiskers
questions.explanation: Outliers are plotted separately; whiskers go to the most extreme non-outliers.
|r| close to 1 means strong; the sign gives the direction.

questions.prompt: The regression line of y on x is y = 2.5x + 4. Predict y when x = 6.

questions.text: To predict x from a given y, use the regression line of x on ___.
questions.explanation: The y-on-x line is not simply rearranged to predict x.

questions.statement: A strong correlation proves that one variable causes the other.
questions.explanation: Correlation is not causation; a third variable may explain both.

questions.prompt: Using a regression line far outside the range of the data is called…
questions.explanation: The linear relationship may not continue beyond the data.

questions.prompt: The regression line is y = 3x − 2 and x̄ = 5. Find ȳ.
questions.explanation: The regression line passes through (x̄, ȳ): 3 × 5 − 2 = 13.

questions.text: Pearson’s r always lies between −1 and ___.
questions.explanation: r = ±1 means all points lie exactly on a straight line.

questions.statement: The y-on-x regression line minimises the sum of the squared vertical distances from the points to the line.

questions.prompt: Match each value of r to its description.
Order these correlation coefficients from weakest to strongest.
questions.explanation: Strength depends on |r|, not on the sign.
